instructions: Fill a large pot with water and bring it to a boil over high heat for the soba.

Meanwhile, wipe the shiitake with a damp towel, cut off and discard the stems, and slice the caps 1/4 inch thick. Cut the root end off the shimeji and pull the clusters apart. Mince the garlic and thinly slice the 3 green onions.
Heat the sesame oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the shiitake and shimeji and cook, stirring now and then, for 6 minutes, until the liquid has cooked off and they're browned in spots.
Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds, until it smells toasty.
Pour in the broth and stir in the soy sauce and mirin. Bring to a boil, then turn the heat down and simmer for 8 minutes.
While the broth simmers, add the soba to the boiling water and cook for 5 minutes, or as the package says. Drain, rinse under cold water, and drain again.
Stir the spinach into the broth and cook for 1 minute, until it's wilted. Take the pot off the heat.
Taste the broth. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Divide the soba among 4 bowls and ladle the broth and mushrooms over it. Top with the green onions and sesame seeds.
method_notes: Lead is Happy Baking Days' kinoko soba (soy, mirin and broth, mushrooms browned in sesame oil, spinach, noodles rinsed and sauced in the bowl); it has no rating and none of the named versions has 20, so this is a fallback. Its mushroom amount is only 1 cup for 4 people, so the mushroom weight follows J-Simple Recipes (shiitake and shimeji, about 11 oz for 2) and the broth is 6 cups for 4 bowls (the lead says 4). Vegetable broth stands in for the dashi in the other sources, which keeps it vegetarian. Its 10 to 15 minute simmer is shortened to 8 to keep the dinner at 30 minutes. Ankake versions thicken the broth with potato starch; this one doesn't.
